"OONO PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT OILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City OPINION NO. MAR 05 HON. PRINCE COLLEN l. JOSON, ET AL. Sangguniang Kabataan Member Barangay United Better Living San Pedro, Laguna Dear SK Member Joson et al: This refers to your letter dated II September 2024 requesting for an opinion on a matter conceming the resignation of Eunice P. Borja, a sangguniang kabataan member (SK member) in your barangay. As represented, SK Member Borja tendered her resignation on II May 2024. It was also mentioned that her resignation was "accepted" by DILG-City Local Govemment Operations Officer (CLGOO) of San Pedro, Laguna on 18 May 2024. From the foregoing facts, these are the issues submitted for our opinion, quoted hereunder in toto: I. 2. 3. 4. 5. Maari po bang bawiin ng isang halal na opisyal ang kanyang pagbibitiw sa tungkulin? Kung maari po sa anong paraan po ito mababawi? At kung hindi naman po ano ang maari naming gawin aksyon patungkol dito? Sino po ba ang dapat tumanggap ng Iiham ng pagbibitiw sa usapin po ng kasapi ng Sangguniang Kabataan? Ito po ba ay irrevocable? We shall answer your ISt to 4th query simultaneously as they are interrelated. The Local Government Code of 19911 (the Code) provides the mechanisms on how to effect the resignation of local elective officials such as sangguniang kabataan members. In particular, Section 82 thereof provides: SECTION 82. Resignation of Elective Local Officials. - (a) Resignations by elective local officials shall be deemed effective only upon acceptance by the following authorities: I Hereinafter referred to as "the Code". "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan•• Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

I) The President, in the case of govemors, vice- governors, and mayors and vice-mayors of highly urbanized cities and independent component cities; 2) The govemor, in the case of municipal mayors, municipal vice- mayors, city mayors and city vice-mayors of component cities; 3) The Sanqqunian concernqg. in the case of Sanqqunian member*: and 4) The city or municipal mayor, in the case of Barangay officials. b.) Copies of the resignation letters of elective local officials, together with the action taken by the aforesaid authorities, shall be furnished the Department of Interior and Local Govemment. c.) The resignation shall be deemed accepted if not acted upon by the authority concemed within fifteen (15) working days from receipt d.) Irrevocable resignations by Sangguniang members shall be deemed accepted upon presentation before an open session of the Sanggunian concemed and duly entered in its records: Provided, however, That this subsection does not apply to Sanggunian members who are subject to recall elections or to cases where existing laws prescribe the manner of acting upon such resignations. As could be clearly gathered from the aforequoted provision, the resignation of a sangguniang kabataan member (SK member) is carried out by tendering resignation to the sangguniang kabataan and shall be deemed effective upon acceptance2 In the case of SK member Borja, we hold that her resignation is not in accordance with the Code. The "acceptance" made by the DILG CLGOO, however, is not the legal acceptance contemplated by law. Her resignation should have been accepted by the sangguniang kabataan as a collegial body to constitute a valid resignation. As regards withdrawal of resignation, the Supreme Court in the case Rubio, Jr. vs Sto. Tomas3 ruled that a resignation may be withdrawn before it is acted upon, but not after acceptance. With respect to your 5th query, Section 82(d) of the Code provides that irrevocable resignation by Sanggunian Kabataan members shall be deemed accepted upon presentation before an open session of the Sanggunian concemed and duly entered in its records The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts 2 See Republic v. Singuin, G.R. No. 149356, 14 March 2008 G.R. No. *3067.
